intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: Construction on NOvA's two massive neutrino detectors began in 2009.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Mirrors experiment:nova: NuMI has had no beam since July 2024 ("The MI has not operated since July 2024", Fermilab PAC, April 2026 meeting).
intervals.quote: 13.6×10²⁰ POT from 555.3 s of integrated beam-pulse time recorded between February 6, 2014, to March 20, 2020

intervals.label: no NuMI beam (Main Injector transformer failures)
intervals.note: Derived from the beam source, as for experiment:nova: NuMI has had no beam since July 2024 and the restart is only planned (Sept 2026 PAC: stable beam planned for 1 October 2026; no later source confirms it). CONFLICTING STATEMENT (left unresolved, status kept): Fermilab's 7 July 2026 feature says NOvA 'is the only currently operating long-baseline neutrino experiment in the United States' and 'is taking data' (https://news.fnal.gov/2026/07/fermilab-marks-70-years-of-neutrino-science-and-leads-next-generation-experiment/); the PAC reports (April and September 2026) are more specific that the Main Injector has not delivered NuMI beam since July 2024, and the feature does not say which data. Shutdown here means no NuMI beam data-taking, not that the detectors are powered down.
intervals.quote: The MI has not operated since July 2024

placements.quote: The 0.3 kt Near Detector is located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target and 100 m underground at Fermilab

depth.quote: The 0.3 kt Near Detector is located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target and 100 m underground at Fermilab

off_axis_angle.quote: Both detectors are centered 14.6 mrad off the beam axis and receive a narrow-band neutrino flux peaked at 1.8 GeV.

overburden.quote: underground at Fermilab, with 22 meters water equivalent overburden

total_mass.note: Conflict: NOvA PRD 106, 032004 describes the near detector as "290 ton"; the NOvA public page and the 2025 monopole paper say 300 t / 0.3 kt.
total_mass.quote: The 0.3 kt Near Detector is located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target and 100 m underground at Fermilab

summary.plain: A small copy of the NOvA far detector, about 300 tonnes, sitting underground at Fermilab a kilometre from where the neutrino beam is made. It measures the beam before the neutrinos have had time to change type.
summary.technical: Functionally identical 0.3 kt PVC-cell liquid-scintillator tracking calorimeter 1 km downstream of the NuMI target and 100 m underground at Fermilab, on the same 14.6 mrad off-axis line as the far detector.

technology.quote: Charged particle tracking is accomplished via PVC cells filled with a mineral oil-based liquid scintillator.
technology.value: segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with liquid scintillator, functionally identical to the far detector
